text:
mike: quick q — for the model entry pipeline, do we require perf bench + safety eval + loader/kv compatibility before we mark a model as "admitted"?
sara: yes, short answer: smoke -> perf -> safety -> full compat. order matters for fast feedback. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jia: +1. my suggestion: lightweight smoke (container + single inference) -> parallel perf jobs (latency + throughput) -> safety/evals -> artifact checks (schema/hashes). keep smoke <30m.
mike: how long do perf jobs take end-to-end? can we parallelize shards so we don't block other onboarding work?
sara: rough numbers: small/quantized models <1h, 7B ~2-4h on a single A100, 70B >8h if full throughput. we can split by sequence-length profile and run parallel workers across instance types. main cost is peak GPU time.
jia: propose we add a quick latency probe we run at submit time to catch immediate regressions (P95 vs baseline). heavier throughput runs can be async and marked as "full profile".
mike: can you paste the smoke job snippet you mentioned?
sara: sure — here's the smoke runner we used in the pilot:
```bash
# smoke.sh
python -m infra.run_smoke --model $MODEL_PATH --input "Hello" --max-tokens 8 --backend cuda --timeout 20
```
It's intentionally tiny, just ensures model loads, runs forward, and returns valid json.
reece: about artifact formats — we need to gate on loader compatibility: acceptable formats = ["pt", "onnx", "gguf", "ggml"], and an API-level loader test: load -> forward -> save-readable-metadata. no silent failures.
jia: compatibility tests I want in the pipeline: load into current runtime, run sample forwards at lengths [8, 512, 2048], warm up kv-cache by simulating incremental decode, quantized load/forward check. If any step crashes or returns NaNs we fail fast.
mike: also add checksums + model-card presence (license + dataset notes) to avoid surprise legal issues.
sara: question on gating numbers: how strict should perf be vs a baseline? 10%? 25%? we don't want to block slightly slower but much cheaper variants.
jia: suggestion: tiered thresholds: admission_warning if P95 <= baseline*1.25 (flag owner), admission_block if P95 > baseline*1.5 OR if safety eval fails. Reward cheaper variants by allowing higher latency if cost per token is lower than baseline by X%.
mike: I like tiered approach. we also should store the raw perf traces in S3 and index them in the console for diffs.
sara: agreed. infra tasks: store traces, attach model-hash, and expose a quick compare UI.
mike: owners? I'll take bench infra (scheduling, parallelism). jia, can you own compat tests and test harness? reece can do artifact validator + policy (formats/licenses).
ja: typo — (jia) I'll own compat. starting tomorrow.
reece: will add format validator and license checks.
onboard-bot: INF-TICKET CREATED: #INF-3912 "model-entry: pipeline checklist + thresholds" (assignee: mike)
mike: I'll open a small RFC/PR with the checklist and proposed Jenkins/GitHub actions today. tagging @sara @jia for review. :thumbsup:
sara: thanks — let's aim to have the RFC + initial CI changes merged before next onboarding wave.
